origin.description: Put up a Windows progress bar widget.
origin.usage: winProgressBar(title = "R progress bar", label = "", min = 0, max = 1, initial = 0, width = 300)

arguments.name: title, label
arguments.text: Window title and dialog label. An empty label omits the label.

arguments.name: min, max, initial
arguments.text: Finite extremes and the starting value.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Width in pixels. NA or a negative width becomes 200.

origin.details: These functions are only available on Windows. This R is Linux, so utils::winProgressBar is not exported.

translation.description: Keep the value, title, and label of a Windows progress bar. No dialog is drawn on this host.
translation.usage: winProgressBar(title="R progress bar", label="", min=0, max=1, initial=0, width=300)

arguments.name: title, label
arguments.text: Stored on the object. An empty label is not updated later.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: A missing or negative width becomes 200, matching the C code.

translation.details: The Win32 window is not created. get and set follow the C state machine.
translation.example:
from utils import winProgressBar
bar = winProgressBar("test progress bar", "Some information", 0, 100, 50)
print(bar.value)
